exposure: genetic factors (family history, siblings/relatives with ASD)
maternal habits during pregnancy (fruit consumption, exclusive breastfeeding, turning off cell phones during sleep)
cohort: The study included 49 children diagnosed with ASD and 100 age-matched controls in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
finding: The study found a significantly higher likelihood of ASD in boys, increased risk with higher maternal education levels, family history of ASD, maternal anxiety during pregnancy, and exposure to vehicle fumes during pregnancy, while frequent fruit consumption, exclusive breastfeeding, and turning off cell phones during sleep were identified as protective factors.
